report.title: Anthropic files confidential S-1 with SEC, targets late-2026 IPO
report.summary: Anthropic submitted a draft Form S-1 on June 1, days after closing a $65B Series H at a $965B valuation — the first major AI lab to formally enter the public-markets process. Revenue run-rate is reported at $47B annualized; share price and count are unset. Builders should note that a publicly-traded Anthropic changes API durability calculus.

report.title: Google kills Gemini CLI for free and Pro users, ships closed-source Antigravity CLI
report.summary: As of June 18, Gemini CLI stopped serving free, Google AI Pro, and Ultra users with no grace period. The replacement is Antigravity CLI (binary: agy) — a closed-source Go rewrite that ships parallel async agents but lacks feature parity at launch, and downgrades quotas from daily to weekly limits. Any CI pipeline calling gemini is broken now.

report.title: Claude Code ships Artifacts, enterprise MCP Okta provisioning, and auto mode on Bedrock/Vertex
report.summary: Claude Code added shareable live Artifacts that auto-update as sessions run — useful for PR walkthroughs and incident pages. Separately, admins can now provision MCP connectors org-wide via Okta with zero-touch user access. Auto mode also landed on Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry for Opus 4.7/4.8.

report.title: OpenAI Codex adds Record & Replay workflow capture and Sites hosted-app builder
report.summary: Codex for macOS Business users can now record a workflow once and replay it as a reusable skill across Computer Use, browser actions, and plugins. Sites (preview) lets Codex deploy web apps and dashboards directly inside the app — ChatGPT Business workspaces get it by default.

report.title: Anthropic poaches AlphaFold's John Jumper from Google DeepMind
report.summary: John Jumper, the Nobel Prize-winning architect of AlphaFold and a VP Engineering Fellow at DeepMind, is joining Anthropic — a significant science talent signal ahead of the company's June 30 science event.

report.title: OpenAI Codex hits 5 million weekly users — 8x growth in five months
report.summary: OpenAI confirmed Codex crossed 5M weekly active users on June 2, up from 600K at the start of 2026, with 20% now knowledge workers rather than developers. The CLI is Apache-2.0, Rust-based, and tops SWE-bench Verified at 88.7% with GPT-5.5.

report.title: Google Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer leaves for IPO-bound OpenAI
report.summary: Noam Shazeer, VP of Engineering and co-lead of Google's Gemini models, announced he is joining OpenAI — arriving the same week that Jumper left DeepMind for Anthropic, underscoring how fast talent is moving between frontier labs ahead of their IPOs.

learn.name: Antigravity CLI (agy)
learn.oneLineDescription: Google's closed-source Go terminal agent that replaced Gemini CLI on June 18.

detail.whatItDoes:
Antigravity CLI is Google's replacement for Gemini CLI, invoked with the binary `agy`. It is a compiled Go binary (no Node.js dependency) that defaults to Gemini 3 Pro and adds parallel async agent orchestration: you can kick off a large-scale refactor or a research task in the background without locking your terminal. It shares a common agent harness with the Antigravity 2.0 desktop app, so improvements to core agents propagate to both.

Key behavioral differences from Gemini CLI: the streaming output format changed from plain text deltas to SSE-formatted events; exit codes are now non-zero on tool-use failures (Gemini CLI exited 0); and MCP server config moved from `~/.gemini/settings.json` (field: `url`) to `~/.antigravity/mcp_config.json` (field: `serverUrl`). Quotas also shifted from a 1,000-requests-per-day cap to a weekly compute cap — heavy users report hitting it mid-workday.
detail.whoItsFor: Any developer who was on a free, Google AI Pro, or Ultra tier using Gemini CLI. Enterprise users on Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise are exempt for now. If your CI pipelines, cron jobs, or shell scripts call `gemini`, you need to audit and replace those calls with `agy` — otherwise they broke on June 18 with no grace period.
pros: Faster execution: single compiled Go binary, no Node.js/npm runtime required
Parallel async sub-agents for complex multi-step tasks without blocking the terminal
Unified harness with Antigravity 2.0 desktop app; agent improvements ship to both simultaneously
Defaults to Gemini 3 Pro instead of gemini-1.5-pro
cons: Closed-source — no Apache 2.0 repo with readable source; GitHub presence is just a changelog and a README
Not at full feature parity with Gemini CLI at launch; some edge-case capabilities may never arrive
Weekly compute quota replaces the old 1,000-requests/day cap; heavy users report hitting it fast
Google has cut usage quotas four times since December 2025 without advance notice
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- A Google account (free, Google AI Pro, or Ultra) OR a paid Gemini API key
- macOS, Linux, or Windows
- **No Node.js required** — agy is a single Go binary

## 1. Remove Gemini CLI (avoids conflicts)

```bash
# If you installed via npm
npm uninstall -g @google/gemini-cli

# Verify it's gone
which gemini  # should return nothing
```

## 2. Install Antigravity CLI

```bash
# macOS / Linux — official install script
curl -sSL https://dl.google.com/antigravity/install.sh | bash

# Or via Homebrew (macOS)
brew install --cask google-antigravity

# Windows — download from the Antigravity release page and add to PATH
# https://cloud.google.com/antigravity/docs/cli/install
```

## 3. Verify the install

```bash
agy --version
# Should print something like: Antigravity CLI 1.x.x
```

## 4. Sign in

```bash
agy auth login
# Opens a browser for Google OAuth — same account as your old Gemini CLI login
```

## 5. Migrate MCP server config (if you used MCP with Gemini CLI)

**Gotcha:** The field name changed from `url` to `serverUrl`. Copying your old config verbatim causes *silent* failures — `agy` starts successfully but MCP tools never connect.

```bash
# Create the new config directory
mkdir -p ~/.antigravity

# Manually migrate your MCP servers:
# OLD: ~/.gemini/settings.json had { "mcpServers": { "myserver": { "url": "..." } } }
# NEW: ~/.antigravity/mcp_config.json needs { "mcpServers": { "myserver": { "serverUrl": "..." } } }

cat > ~/.antigravity/mcp_config.json << 'EOF'
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "my-mcp-server": {
      "serverUrl": "http://localhost:3000"
    }
  }
}
EOF
```

**Verify MCP actually connected** — don't just check that `agy` starts:

```bash
agy "list the tools you have available from MCP"
# If MCP is broken, you'll get no tools listed despite a clean startup
```

## 6. Fix your automation scripts

```bash
# Find every place you call gemini in scripts, GitHub Actions, Makefiles, cron:
grep -r 'gemini ' ~/.bashrc ~/.zshrc ~/scripts/ .github/ Makefile 2>/dev/null

# Replace:
# BEFORE: gemini "do something"
# AFTER:  agy "do something"
```

## Gotchas
- **Streaming format changed**: scripts that parse `--stream` output (plain text deltas in Gemini CLI) now receive SSE-formatted events from `agy`. Rewrite any parsers.
- **Exit codes changed**: Gemini CLI exited 0 on tool-use failures; `agy` exits non-zero. CI pipelines with `set -e` will now halt on previously-silent errors.
- **Weekly quota**: Parallel agents consume quota faster than single-turn calls. Monitor with `agy quota status`.
- **State directory moved**: `~/.gemini/agents/` → `~/.antigravity/agents/` — existing agent state is not auto-migrated.

learn.name: Claude Code Artifacts
learn.oneLineDescription: Turn any Claude Code session into a live, shareable, auto-updating web page.

detail.whatItDoes:
Claude Code Artifacts let a running session publish its work as a live web page that updates in place as the session progresses. The artifact can be a PR walkthrough, an incident timeline, a dashboard (filterable and sortable), a release checklist that fills itself out, or a system architecture explainer. It draws from the session's full context — codebase, connected MCP tools, and conversation — without requiring separate data wiring.

Every publish creates a new version at the same link, with version history so teammates can restore a prior state. Sharing is private by default (org-only) on Team and Enterprise plans. The artifact updates live: anyone with the link sees changes the moment Claude Code publishes them.
detail.whoItsFor: Engineering teams and tech leads who currently write status updates, incident reports, or PR descriptions by hand after a Claude Code session. Also useful for solo developers who want a living document that tracks what an agent session changed and why — especially helpful for long-running refactors or incident investigations where context would otherwise be lost in terminal scroll.
pros: Zero infrastructure: Claude Code builds and hosts the artifact from session context — no separate dashboard tooling required
Live updates: open page refreshes in place as the session progresses, so no manual re-sharing
Version history lets you restore any prior published state from the gallery
Combines code, MCP connector data, and reasoning in one page — e.g. failing test + error spike from monitoring + root-cause from the session
cons: Private org-only sharing and version history are in beta — availability varies by plan
Artifact quality depends on how well the session was structured; poorly-scoped sessions produce poorly-structured artifacts
No custom domain or export to PDF/HTML yet at launch
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Claude Code v2.1.150+ (run `claude --version` to check; update with `claude update`)
- Claude Team, Enterprise, or pay-as-you-go plan (Artifacts sharing scope varies by plan)

## 1. Update Claude Code

```bash
claude update
claude --version
# Should be v2.1.150 or higher
```

## 2. Create an artifact during a session

Start any session and ask Claude to publish an artifact:

```bash
claude
```

Then inside the session:

```
> Refactor the auth module to use the new JWT library, then create an artifact summarizing what changed, why, and any migration steps the team needs.
```

Claude Code will run the refactor and then publish a live page.

## 3. Ask for specific artifact types

```
# PR walkthrough
> Create a PR walkthrough artifact for these changes.

# Incident page (combine MCP monitoring data + code context)
> Create an incident artifact covering the error spike we just diagnosed.

# Release checklist that auto-fills
> Create a release checklist artifact for v2.4.0 and check off each item as we complete it.
```

## 4. Browse and manage your artifacts

```bash
# Inside a Claude Code session:
/artifacts
# Opens the gallery showing all published artifacts with version history
```

## Gotchas
- **Artifacts are org-only by default**: the shareable link requires the recipient to be in your Claude org. Public sharing is not available at launch.
- **Version history is in beta**: if you don't see it, check your plan tier and wait for the beta to roll out to your org.
- **MCP connector data requires active connectors**: if your session doesn't have MCP tools connected, artifacts won't include external data (monitoring, Jira, etc.). Set up connectors first via the Claude web app Settings → Connectors.

learn.name: OpenAI Codex CLI (Record & Replay)
learn.oneLineDescription: Demonstrate a workflow once on macOS; Codex turns it into a reusable skill automatically.

detail.whatItDoes:
Codex CLI is OpenAI's open-source (Apache-2.0), Rust-based coding agent for the terminal. The June 2026 release adds Record & Replay: on macOS, Business users can record a workflow — clicking through a UI, filling forms, running commands — and Codex captures it as a reusable skill that can be replayed via Computer Use, browser actions, plugins, or any combination. It is most useful for stable, repeatable workflows that are easier to demonstrate than describe (e.g., creating a configured issue in a project tracker, publishing a video, downloading a recurring report).

The CLI also added a Sites plugin (preview) that lets Codex deploy web apps, dashboards, and internal tools directly to OpenAI-hosted infrastructure from inside the terminal. The underlying model is GPT-5.5, which holds the highest SWE-bench Verified score (88.7%) of any coding agent as of June 2026. Context window is 256K tokens (standard) or 1M tokens with GPT-5.4.
detail.whoItsFor: Developers and technical product teams on ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, or Enterprise plans who run repetitive cross-app workflows. Record & Replay specifically targets tasks that are painful to script but trivial to click through once. Also relevant for teams evaluating Codex as an alternative to Claude Code — the Rust rewrite, sandboxed shell execution, and GPT-5.5 integration make it a competitive option.
pros: Record & Replay captures GUI workflows without writing automation scripts — show it once, reuse indefinitely
Open-source (Apache-2.0) and Rust-built: fast startup, low memory, readable source at github.com/openai/codex
Shell commands run in a sandboxed container by default — can't touch the rest of your machine without explicit approval
GPT-5.5 default model scores 88.7% on SWE-bench Verified, essentially tied with Claude Opus 4.8
cons: Record & Replay requires Computer Use enabled, and is currently macOS-only; excluded from EU, UK, Switzerland
Full feature set (Codex app, Sites, Computer Use) requires Business or higher plan — CLI is included in Plus/Pro but advanced features are gated
Sites plugin is preview-only; not suitable for production traffic yet
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- macOS, Linux, or Windows
- ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, or Enterprise subscription (OR an OpenAI API key)
- Node.js 18+ for npm install path; or use the standalone installer (no Node.js needed)
- For Record & Replay: macOS, ChatGPT Business or higher, Computer Use enabled by your org admin

## 1. Install Codex CLI

```bash
# Option A: npm (requires Node 18+)
npm install -g @openai/codex

# Option B: standalone installer (macOS/Linux, no Node dependency)
curl -fsSL https://cdn.openai.com/codex/install.sh | bash

# Option C: Homebrew (macOS)
brew install --cask codex

# Verify
codex --version
```

## 2. Authenticate

```bash
codex
# First run prompts for sign-in.
# Choose: ChatGPT account (browser OAuth) OR API key

# To use an API key directly:
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
codex
```

## 3. Run your first task

```bash
# Interactive TUI session
codex

# One-shot non-interactive (good for scripts)
codex exec "add input validation to the signup form in src/auth.ts"

# Switch model inside TUI
# Type: /model
# Then select from the picker (GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.2-Codex, etc.)
```

## 4. Set up Record & Replay (macOS Business only)

```
# Inside the Codex macOS app (not CLI):
# 1. Ensure Computer Use is enabled: Settings → Computer Use → Enable
# 2. Click the Record button (top bar) to start capturing
# 3. Perform the workflow you want to automate
# 4. Click Stop — Codex names and saves the skill
# 5. Use the skill: open the skill picker and select it, or reference it in a prompt
```

## 5. Run Codex in fully automated mode (CI/CD)

```bash
# --full-auto skips all approval prompts — use only in sandboxed CI environments
codex exec --full-auto "run the test suite and fix any failing tests"

# For unattended installs:
CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=1 bash install.sh
```

## Gotchas
- **Approval mode matters**: default mode asks before every file write or shell command. `--full-auto` removes that gate — only use it in disposable CI containers.
- **Record & Replay is excluded from EU/UK/Switzerland** at initial launch; check your region before planning workflows around it.
- **API key vs. ChatGPT login**: logging in via ChatGPT gives you GPT-5.5 and the full 256K context. An API key defaults to GPT-5.2-Codex and bills per token — check which you want before starting.
- **Sites plugin (preview)**: enable it from the Codex app sidebar → Sites. Hosted environment variables and secrets are managed per-site in the UI.

learn.name: Bumblebee
learn.oneLineDescription: Read-only supply chain scanner for npm, PyPI, MCP servers, VS Code extensions from Perplexity AI.

detail.whatItDoes:
Bumblebee is a read-only supply chain security scanner from Perplexity AI written in Go 1.25 with zero non-standard library dependencies. In a single pass it scans npm packages, PyPI packages, Go modules, RubyGems, Composer packages, MCP servers, VS Code extensions, and browser extensions for suspicious or malicious packages. Because it is read-only by design and makes no unexpected network calls, it can be safely added to CI pipelines and developer laptops without introducing new attack surface.

The motivation is direct: the AI tooling era has dramatically expanded the supply chain attack surface. MCP servers are often installed by clicking a Discord link. Editor extensions have full filesystem access. Browser extensions see every page. Bumblebee audits all of these at once instead of requiring separate tools per ecosystem.
detail.whoItsFor: Security-conscious developers and DevSecOps teams who install MCP servers, editor extensions, or AI tooling from third-party sources. Useful as a pre-commit hook or CI step for any team that has expanded its AI tool footprint in 2025-2026 and wants a fast audit of what is actually in the dependency graph.
pros: Single binary, zero runtime dependencies — trivial to add to any CI pipeline or developer machine
Covers MCP servers and editor extensions, not just traditional package ecosystems
Read-only by design — cannot modify files or make unexpected outbound calls
Written in Go 1.25 with zero non-standard library dependencies: easy to audit the scanner itself
cons: Backed by Perplexity AI — longevity and update cadence depend on Perplexity's prioritization
Detection quality depends on the threat intelligence database; novel or very new malicious packages may not be flagged yet
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- macOS or Linux (Windows support: check the README)
- No runtime dependencies — single binary

## 1. Install Bumblebee

```bash
# macOS via Homebrew
brew install perplexity-ai/tap/bumblebee

# Linux: download the binary directly
curl -fsSL https://github.com/perplexity-ai/bumblebee/releases/latest/download/bumblebee-linux-amd64 \
  -o /usr/local/bin/bumblebee
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/bumblebee

# Verify
bumblebee --version
```

## 2. Scan your current project

```bash
# From your project root — scans all detected package manifests
bumblebee scan .

# Scan a specific ecosystem
bumblebee scan --npm .
bumblebee scan --pypi .
bumblebee scan --mcp ~/.claude/mcp_config.json
```

## 3. Scan editor extensions and MCP servers

```bash
# VS Code extensions
bumblebee scan --vscode

# MCP servers (Claude Code config)
bumblebee scan --mcp ~/.claude/mcp_config.json

# Everything at once
bumblebee scan --all
```

## 4. Add to CI (GitHub Actions example)

```yaml
# .github/workflows/supply-chain.yml
name: Supply Chain Scan
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  bumblebee:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install Bumblebee
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/perplexity-ai/bumblebee/releases/latest/download/bumblebee-linux-amd64 \
            -o /usr/local/bin/bumblebee
          chmod +x /usr/local/bin/bumblebee
      - name: Scan dependencies
        run: bumblebee scan --all .
```

## Gotchas
- **MCP server scanning requires the config file path**: Bumblebee doesn't auto-discover MCP configs; pass the path explicitly with `--mcp <path>`.
- **Browser extension scanning may require elevated permissions** on some platforms to read the extensions directory.
- **Read-only means no auto-remediation**: Bumblebee flags issues but does not remove packages. You act on the report manually.

learn.name: anthropics/claude-plugins-official
learn.oneLineDescription: Anthropic's managed GitHub directory of production-ready Claude Code plugins (30k+ stars).

detail.whatItDoes:
claude-plugins-official is the Anthropic-managed GitHub repository that serves as the official marketplace for Claude Code plugins. Plugins are packages that add domain-specific skills, slash commands, MCP server connectors, subagents, hooks, and LSP support on top of Claude Code. Each plugin is implemented as markdown and JSON — no build steps, no compiled code — making them readable and customizable by anyone.

The official library covers productivity (Slack, Notion, Linear), sales (HubSpot, Clay, ZoomInfo), customer support (ticket triage, knowledge base), legal, finance, data, and security (Security Guidance, Semgrep). As of June 1, 2026, the top plugins by installs were Frontend Design (829K installs), Superpowers (752K installs), and Context7 (348K installs). The separately maintained anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins repo covers 11 production knowledge-work plugins (sales, legal, finance, data, product management) at 17K+ stars.
detail.whoItsFor: Any Claude Code user who wants to extend the tool with domain-specific context, external service connectors, or repeatable slash commands — without writing code. Particularly useful for team leads who want to standardize how an entire team interacts with Claude Code (same skills, same hooks, same MCP connectors installed from one place).
pros: Anthropic-managed quality bar — official plugins are reviewed and maintained by the team that builds Claude Code
Zero-code plugin format: skills and commands are plain markdown files any team member can read and customize
Directly installable from inside Claude Code via /plugin marketplace or the /plugin init scaffold command
Covers the full stack from LSP code intelligence to external service connectors (Jira, Figma, Supabase, etc.)
cons: Official library is curated and slow-moving — community plugins in third-party repos move faster but lack quality guarantees
Plugin executables run on the Bash tool PATH — review any plugin that includes executable scripts before installing in a sensitive environment
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Claude Code v2.1.145+ (run `claude --version`; update with `claude update`)
- Claude account (plugins require API or subscription access; no free tier for Claude Code)

## 1. Browse the official marketplace inside Claude Code

```bash
claude
# Then inside the TUI:
/plugin
# Opens the Discover tab showing the official marketplace
```

## 2. Install a plugin directly by name

```bash
# Inside a Claude Code session:
/plugin install security-guidance
/plugin install context7
/plugin install frontend-design

# Or from the CLI before starting a session:
claude --plugin-dir ~/.claude/plugins/security-guidance
```

## 3. Install the full official library from GitHub

```bash
# Clone the official plugin repo
git clone https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official.git ~/.claude/official-plugins

# Point Claude Code at it (one-time setup in settings.json)
cat >> ~/.claude/settings.json << 'EOF'
{
  "pluginMarketplaces": [
    { "source": "~/.claude/official-plugins", "name": "official" }
  ]
}
EOF
```

## 4. Install the knowledge-work plugins (sales, legal, finance, data)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins.git ~/.claude/knowledge-work

# Then inside Claude Code:
/plugin install --dir ~/.claude/knowledge-work/sales
/plugin install --dir ~/.claude/knowledge-work/legal
```

## 5. Scaffold a custom plugin for your team

```bash
# Inside a Claude Code session:
/plugin init my-team-workflow
# Creates ~/.claude/skills/my-team-workflow/ with a CLAUDE.md template
# Edit the markdown to add your team's skills, then /plugin install it
```

## Gotchas
- **Plugin hooks run as shell commands**: any plugin with PostToolUse or PreToolUse hooks executes shell code on your machine. Read the hook definitions in the plugin's CLAUDE.md before installing.
- **Marketplace auto-loads on session start**: if a plugin update breaks something, run `/plugin marketplace update claude-plugins-official` to refresh, or `--safe-mode` to start with all plugins disabled for debugging.
- **`/plugin list` shows installed plugins inline** (added in v2.1.157) — use this to audit what is active in a session before running sensitive tasks.
